modules.name: Layer 0 schema, versioning and open-schema mapping
modules.design_question: What minimum geometry-plus-program record, versioned and staged, lets every module read one design consistently, including storeys, voids, podium and access points, and export to IFC, Speckle, glTF and BOT?
modules.effort: M: core schema v0 (schema_version, FloorPlate with has_floor, Ajv validation, one migration stub), JSON and GLB-with-extras export about 3.5 person-days; v1: IFC4 ADD2 exporter about 2, BOT mapper 1, Speckle 2026.9 mapper 2 (team estimate)
inputs: Class and port-type definitions (JSON Schema files) proposed by modules, each with a schema_version
Program-tag vocabulary (office, residential, hotel, retail, cultural/civic, public, amenity, mechanical, core), published as one local IfcClassification
Any staged Layer 0 document (Draft, Georef, Checked, Complete) passed in by callers for validation, migration or export; M01 is a schema package with no canvas ports
outputs: Layer 0 JSON Schema (Z-up, right-handed, metres) with semver schema_version and typed ports: Site, Podium, Tower, Level (negative elevations below grade), ProgramVolume, FloorPlate (has_floor), OpenSpace, Frontage, AccessPoint, Viewpoint, ViewCone, ContextBuilding, Assumption
Staged document types, each produced by one module: Layer0Draft (M02), Layer0Georef (M03), Layer0Checked (M05), Layer0Complete (M04)
Mapping table: each class to its IFC, Speckle, glTF and BOT target with status mapped, custom property set or missing
Pure exporter functions: GLB with node extras (core); IFC4 ADD2 (IfcSite > IfcBuilding > IfcBuildingStorey > IfcSpace, IfcSpatialZone), BOT Turtle graph and Speckle 2026.9 version (v1)
Migration functions vN to vN+1 with CI fixtures; result-card provenance fields (source_id, snapshot hash, schema_version)

parameters.name: Spatial hierarchy and shared podium
parameters.relationship: A storey belongs to one building; composition types COMPLEX/ELEMENT/PARTIAL let a shared podium be a PARTIAL section. Zones may overlap, so tower footprints on podium levels use IfcSpatialZone. Finer records enable per-floor metrics but raise tagging effort.

parameters.name: Storey slicing, voids and mezzanines
parameters.relationship: Slicing a volume on the storey schedule gives per-floor area, but atria, double-height lobbies and sky gardens would count as floors, inflating gross and FSR area. A has_floor flag lists void area apart; mezzanines map to PARTIAL storeys.

parameters.name: Program vocabulary (9 tags)
parameters.relationship: More tags split uses finely but each needs a classification entry. Tags roll up to the brief's use groups and travel as IfcClassificationReference to a declared local IfcClassification, readable by IFC tools, not only as a custom property.

parameters.name: FSR-counted area and denominator
parameters.relationship: The 9.0 FSR minimum is about 103,200 m2 on 11,468 m2 (derived). Gross versus counted area, exclusions, employment flags and the denominator (brief rectangle, polygon or net parcel) each move the shortfall; 1% of the denominator is about 1,032 m2. By-law wording is unread.

parameters.name: Geometry carrier (display mesh vs exact B-rep)
parameters.relationship: Triangle meshes approximate curved faces, so area and volume error grows with tessellation tolerance; exact B-rep keeps volume but is heavy in a browser. Speckle's earlier object graph likewise separated display meshes from source objects.

parameters.name: Z origin, vertical datum and height definition
parameters.relationship: Tower height and storey count depend on where Z = 0 sits; CTBUH measures from the lowest significant open-air entrance. Z0 also needs a geodetic elevation and datum so City context and view limits stated as elevations line up.

parameters.name: Identity scheme (GlobalId, applicationId, own hash)
parameters.relationship: Stable ids let tags, versions and diffs survive re-import. IFC rooted entities carry a GlobalId; Speckle 2026.9 keys objects by applicationId (the older graph used content hashes). Layer 0 stores GlobalId, applicationId, its own SHA-256 and a UUID separately.

parameters.name: Internal frame (metres, Z-up, right-handed)
parameters.relationship: glTF fixes metres and +Y up, while Layer 0 is Z-up like Rhino and IFC authoring (convention, not checked here). The GLB exporter rotates the root node -90 degrees about X; a missed rotation lays the tower on its side and corrupts sun-direction tests.

parameters.name: IFC export baseline and elevation attributes
parameters.relationship: IfcOpenShell claims extensive geometry support only for IFC2x3 and IFC4 Add2. IFC4 ADD2 export writes storey Elevation, IfcBuilding.ElevationOfRefHeight (Z0 geodetic) and IfcSite.RefElevation, which IFC4.3 deprecates (ADD2 inferred). IFC4X3 waits for a round-trip pass.

parameters.name: Schema version and migration
parameters.relationship: A MAJOR change breaks stored snapshots, result-card replays and forked modules unless every document and port type carries schema_version and a tested migration vN to vN+1. Module manifests pin the port schema; replay migrates first, then compares hashes.

parameters.name: Targets for non-spatial classes
parameters.relationship: OpenSpace stays an external IfcSpace under IfcSite. Frontage, AccessPoint, Viewpoint and ViewCone map to IfcAnnotation with a custom pset; ContextBuilding to an IfcBuilding under a separate context IfcSite; Assumption to IfcDocumentReference. BOT has no such classes, so a vtc: namespace extends it.

metrics.name: Mandatory-field completeness
metrics.good: 100% of fields required at the document's stage present: Draft (geometry, source unit); Georef (site polygon, Z0 geodetic elevation and datum, north record and type); Complete (at least one tower, storeys with elevation, every volume tagged, has_floor set)
metrics.bad: Any gap: dependent modules show a provisional label
metrics.method: Ajv JSON Schema validation on every write, with the required list chosen by stage
metrics.basis: Required fields are our own schema v0 definition

metrics.name: IFC round-trip fidelity (v1)
metrics.good: 100% of ids, tags, units, axis assertion, storey Elevation, ElevationOfRefHeight, RefElevation, plate-to-storey and zone-to-plate links survive IFC4 ADD2 export then re-import with IfcOpenShell and web-ifc; IFC4X3 reported separately
metrics.bad: Any tag, id, unit, elevation or link lost
metrics.method: Automated test on each test model, including a tower, diffing before and after
metrics.basis: Team test criterion; IFC4X3 geometry support unverified (IfcOpenShell README)

metrics.name: Mapping coverage
metrics.good: Every Layer 0 class has an IFC, Speckle 2026.9, glTF and BOT target documented (13 of 13)
metrics.bad: Any class without a documented target
metrics.method: Coverage matrix generated from the mapping table
metrics.basis: Own mapping table. r1 left six classes without targets and the zone-to-space direction open; r2 adds targets for all 13 classes and confirms IfcSpatialZone as RelatingStructure of IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure (IFC4.3 pages; FALSE_ASSUMPTION r2 flag)

metrics.name: Schema migration replay
metrics.good: 100% of stored fixtures migrate to the current schema_version and re-validate; replayed output hashes match after migration
metrics.bad: Any fixture fails to migrate, validate or hash
metrics.method: CI runs every stored fixture through the migration chain, then validates and replays result cards
metrics.basis: Team rule; semver defines MAJOR as a breaking change

visualization: Schema browser: tree Site > Podium/Tower > Level > Volume > FloorPlate with object counts and void share per volume
Coverage matrix: rows are Layer 0 classes, columns IFC / Speckle / glTF / BOT; green mapped, amber custom property set, red missing
Type badges on canvas node ports with a schema_version chip; clicking a badge opens the schema clause and its source
Stage ribbon Draft > Georef > Checked > Complete showing which module produced the current document
modules.method: Define Layer 0 as a JSON Schema validated with Ajv, with semver schema_version and one tested migration function per version. Documents are staged (Draft from M02, Georef from M03, Checked from M05, Complete from M04), so the module graph stays acyclic; CI checks that and that each depends_on equals the producers of its inputs. Mapping: Site to IfcSite and bot:Site; Podium and Tower to IfcBuilding (PARTIAL sections) and bot:Building; Level to IfcBuildingStorey; ProgramVolume to IfcSpatialZone and bot:Zone, linked to storeys by bot:intersectsZone and to its plates by bot:containsZone; FloorPlate to IfcSpace, referenced by the zone through IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure. Tags become IfcClassificationReference, areas Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities, project flags a custom pset not named Pset_. Exporters are pure functions; CI re-imports every export with IfcOpenShell and web-ifc and diffs.
modules.human_judgment: Which tag a volume gets, which tags count as non-residential employment area, which levels of a volume have floors, how storeys and the entrance Z0 are defined, and what counts toward FSR stay with the designer; the schema only records the decision and its origin.
modules.limits: Mapping massing volumes to IfcSpatialZone and IfcSpace is a convention. IFC4.3 pages were read (zone-space relation, PARTIAL storeys, deprecations); IFC4 ADD2 pages were not, so ADD2 behaviour is inferred until the round-trip spike. BOT is a W3C public draft with no stated licence. EXT_structural_metadata is a Cesium draft, so v0 uses plain glTF extras. Speckle 2026.9 site and building containers are undocumented. Schema v0 will change after VTC test models.

modules.name: Multi-format import pipeline
modules.design_question: Which route gets each file type (.3dm, OBJ, IFC, glTF/FBX, DXF/DWG, SketchUp, Revit) into Layer 0 with units, hierarchy, metadata and meshes preserved, and what is lost on each?
modules.effort: L: core .3dm, OBJ, GLB adapters about 3.5 person-days; fallback mesher 2; IFC (web-ifc) adapter and SketchUp/Revit export cards 1.5 (after 6 Nov); v1: FBX and DXF 2D route about 2, Speckle 2026.9 and APS routes about 4 (team estimate)
inputs: Uploaded file (.3dm, .obj, .ifc/.ifczip, .glb/.gltf; v1: .fbx, .dxf; via export: .skp, .rvt, .dwg)
User-declared source unit (mandatory for OBJ)
Layer or name filter
Tessellation tolerance
outputs: Layer0Draft: meshes, raw property bag per object, mesh source label (cached, prism, planar, subd-net or none), source provenance
Import report: objects read, skipped and why, units, warnings, unmeshed objects (blocking for ProgramVolumes)
Source-file hash for P14-M06
Raw layer paths, names and IFC classes for P14-M04
Fixture manifest: organiser 'Site plans & 3D model' once obtained, plus 5 VTC-style test massings (including an extrusion-only file and a no-render-mesh file) run in CI

parameters.name: Source unit
parameters.relationship: OBJ stores no unit, so a wrong guess scales the model by 1,000 (mm) or 3.28 (ft) and breaks the 244-305 m range. rhino3dm exposes ModelUnitSystem, glTF is metres, and SketchUp's OBJ export has a unit drop-down.

parameters.name: Render meshes in .3dm files
parameters.relationship: openNURBS cannot tessellate Breps, so Brep faces need meshes saved in the file; extrusions and SubDs expose the same cached meshes (Extrusion getMesh, SubD control net). Files saved without meshes need the fallback mesher or an export from Rhino.

parameters.name: Fallback mesher route
parameters.relationship: Polyline extrusions become exact prisms; planar Brep faces are triangulated from edge loops with earcut and area-checked; SubDs use the control net (volume biased); curved Breps need Rhino meshes. Coarser curve sampling cuts triangles but adds area error.

parameters.name: Import route per format
parameters.relationship: Native readers exist for 3dm, OBJ, IFC and glTF. SketchUp and Revit need a vendor export or connector, which adds a user step but keeps names, layers and properties. DWG/DXF 2D plans need a Rhino 8 conversion or a DXF parser.

parameters.name: IFC schema of the incoming file (2x3 / 4 / 4x3)
parameters.relationship: web-ifc enumerates IFC2X3, IFC4 and IFC4X3, but IfcOpenShell claims extensive geometry support only for IFC2x3 and IFC4 Add2. Ask authors for IFC4 and do not send IFC4X3 to the server fallback until the round-trip spike passes.

parameters.name: Layer and name filter
parameters.relationship: Dropping furniture, annotation and context layers cuts triangles and mis-tagging; keeping everything preserves provenance but slows load and pollutes floor-area sums.

parameters.name: Metadata retention
parameters.relationship: Retained properties feed P14-M04 labelling. Connectors differ: Rhino sends name, colour, user strings; SketchUp custom attributes; Revit category, family, type, level and parameters.

parameters.name: Organiser model format (unknown)
parameters.relationship: The page lists 'Site plans & 3D model' with no formats, and its download links still point to '#' (21 Oct). If it is .skp or .dwg, no core adapter reads it, so entrants need a Rhino 8 or SketchUp conversion first.

metrics.name: Object accounting
metrics.good: 100% of source objects imported or listed as skipped with a reason
metrics.method: Count source objects against imported plus skipped
metrics.basis: Team rule: nothing disappears without a record

metrics.name: ProgramVolumes without usable mesh
metrics.good: 0 after the fallback mesher
metrics.method: Count ProgramVolume-class objects whose mesh source label is none
metrics.basis: Corrects the r1 UNVERIFIED claim: openNURBS has no tessellation, but Extrusion getMesh/setMesh/toBrep and Mesh.createFromSubDControlNet are bound, so a deterministic fallback exists. Team rule that a missing tower must never pass silently, since FSR and height checks would run on an empty model

metrics.name: Fallback mesher area error
metrics.good: <= 0.1% of source-reported area for planar faces (earcut deviation check)
metrics.method: Compare triangulated area with the polygon area per face and with the Rhino-reported area
metrics.basis: Team presets; earcut gives no correctness guarantee on invalid rings but reports a deviation

metrics.name: Volume parity with source application
metrics.good: <= 1% difference between imported mesh volume and source-reported volume
metrics.method: Compare signed mesh volume with the volume the user reads from Rhino, SketchUp or IFC quantities
metrics.basis: Team assumption; no source threshold found

metrics.name: IFC import time (<= 50 MB, mid-range laptop)
metrics.good: <= 10 s to meshes, in a worker
metrics.method: Time web-ifc open plus mesh extraction on a VTC-sized test model on a mid-range Windows laptop
metrics.basis: web-ifc benchmark on an Apple M1: files of 26-70 MB opened in 0.17-1.16 s and executed in 0.52-7.6 s; time does not track size (47 MB in 0.52 s, 34 MB in 7.6 s). Thresholds are padded presets to be replaced by our own measurement (r1 subset quote is a FALSE ASSUMPTION flag)

metrics.name: UI responsiveness during import (INP p75)
metrics.method: Event timing for clicks and key presses while a worker imports (INP does not observe drags or scrolling)
metrics.basis: web.dev INP thresholds

metrics.name: Peak memory of an import
metrics.good: <= 50% of the WASM module's declared maximum memory
metrics.method: Compare memory.buffer.byteLength with the module's declared maximum, read from the WASM binary, during imports
metrics.basis: Team presets. Memory64 is stable in Chrome 133 and Firefox 134 but only a Safari Technical Preview, so Safari and each module's own maximum bind (r1 4 GiB ceiling is a FALSE ASSUMPTION flag)

visualization: Import report panel: one row per source object with status chips (imported, merged, skipped, unmeshed) and reason
Unit-detection banner showing candidate scales and the resulting selected-polygon bounding box against 79.2 x 144.8 m
3D preview coloured by import status (green ok, amber heuristic or fallback mesh, red skipped or unmeshed) with a triangle-count-per-layer bar chart
Dated supported-formats table in the import dialog; each row links to its how-to card and lists what is lost
modules.method: Sniff format, then run an adapter in a Web Worker that emits one ImportedObject list. .3dm: rhino3dm File3dm read, layer paths, names, attributes, instance definitions, ModelUnitSystem, EarthAnchorPoint; use saved meshes via BrepFace.getMesh and Extrusion.getMesh, else the fallback mesher (prism, earcut planar faces, SubD control net) and a blocking report line for unmeshed ProgramVolumes. IFC: web-ifc mesh streaming plus property sets for IFC2x3 and IFC4; IfcOpenShell server fallback for oversized files; IFC4X3 after the spike. OBJ: groups and usemtl, unit required. glTF/GLB: three.js GLTFLoader, read extras. FBX and DXF: v1, unit prompt. SKP and RVT: accept exported OBJ/GLB/IFC or Speckle versions with an export how-to card. The result is Layer0Draft; P14-M03 then adds units and georeference.
modules.human_judgment: Choosing the source unit when detection is ambiguous, deciding which layers are building versus context or clutter, accepting skipped objects and fallback meshes, and re-exporting from Rhino when a curved Brep has no mesh.
modules.limits: Browsers cannot read .skp or .rvt: the SketchUp C SDK needs registration and Trimble terms; Revit is proprietary. Curved Breps without saved meshes cannot be meshed here (openNURBS has no tessellation). McNeel says core-hour billing (USD 0.10) is incompatible with Educational and Commercial licences; Rhino.Compute workstation use is unverified. OBJ loses hierarchy and metadata. Speckle connectors transfer no image textures.

modules.name: Units, true north and georeferencing
modules.design_question: Where is the model and which way is north? Fix units, anchor the site in EPSG:3157 with a geodetic Z0, and reconcile the plan's arrow with true north.
modules.effort: S-M: core unit check, four-way north confirmation, site polygon and frontage, CRS and Z0 record about 2 person-days; v1: IfcMapConversion export, parcel-derived street bearing, WMM evaluator and LiDAR frame test about 1.5 more (team estimate)
inputs: Layer0Draft and import report (declared units)
User-selected site polygon or tower object for scale detection; site boundary polygon, street frontage lines (with street type) and access points drawn by the user
North arrow bearing: two points clicked on the plan, or IFC TrueNorth, or Rhino ModelNorth; plus the north type declared by the user: true, magnetic, projection (UTM) grid or street-grid (plan)
Any IfcMapConversion / IfcProjectedCRS in the file, Rhino EarthAnchorPoint, and the entrance-level Z0 geodetic elevation
Optional (v1, from P14-M08): parcel polygons, derived street-grid bearing and LiDAR ground at the entrance
outputs: Layer0Georef with a georeference record: crs EPSG:3157 (EPSG:26910 accepted as alias with a warning), datum-shift option (null or EPSG 1946 position-vector) and its test result, origin easting/northing, z0_geodetic_m, vertical_datum, true_north_deg, north_type, magnetic_declination_deg (model, epoch), grid_convergence_deg, ground_to_grid_scale (Layer 0 and custom pset only), LoGeoRef level
Unit scale factor applied
Street-grid bearing (default 44.7 and 134.7 degrees from true north, derived; live value from P14-M08)
IfcMapConversion (Scale 1.0, OrthogonalHeight = Z0) and IfcProjectedCRS (VerticalDatum); IfcMapConversionScaled for IFC4X3; local-to-map 4x4 matrix
True-north vector for sun and wind modules, released only after the north type is confirmed and the street-edge check passes or is waived

parameters.name: Declared source unit
parameters.relationship: Scales every coordinate: a mm/m slip changes tower height 1,000-fold, ft/m 3.28-fold. Detection tests candidate scales on the user-selected site polygon or tower against 79.2 x 144.8 m, never the whole file, and the user confirms with one click.

parameters.name: North type (true, magnetic, projection grid, street-grid)
parameters.relationship: Magnetic, UTM grid and street-grid north differ from true north by about 15.4, 0.09 and 44.7 degrees here (derived). Picking UTM 'grid' for a street-grid arrow leaves about 44.6 degrees unapplied, so CLIM modules stay blocked until the user confirms.

parameters.name: True-north angle (model north vs +Y)
parameters.relationship: Rotates every sun-path, shadow and wind result by the same angle. For a 300 m tower at latitude 49.29 N, 1 degree moves the shadow tip about 6 m at equinox noon and about 17 m at winter-solstice noon (derived).

parameters.name: Magnetic declination (WMM2025)
parameters.relationship: Declination at the site and date converts a magnetic arrow to true north. Our WMM2025 evaluation gives about 15.4 degrees east for October 2026 (derived; it reproduces pygeomag's Seattle example). The tool records model, epoch and uncertainty; WMM2025 is valid to late 2029.

parameters.name: Street-grid bearing (parcel edges)
parameters.relationship: Parcel edges within 700 m of 49.283 N, 123.121 W run at about 44.7 and 134.7 degrees from true north (derived, 969 parcels). A model aligned to the street grid must still carry true north separately, or sun and wind results rotate by about 45 degrees.

parameters.name: Horizontal CRS and datum shift
parameters.relationship: Use EPSG:3157 NAD83(CSRS) / UTM 10N (City LiDAR frame). A null shift versus EPSG 1946 with arc-second position-vector rotations differs by about 1.3 m here; the epsg.io string as copied drops its rotations and errs about 0.9 m (both derived).

parameters.name: Z0 geodetic elevation and vertical datum
parameters.relationship: City footprint heights are geodetic and LiDAR uses CGVD28GVRD, and view limits are elevations, so Z0 must be stored as a geodetic height plus datum, not a bare local zero. Default it from LiDAR ground at the entrance; the user confirms.

parameters.name: Ground-to-grid scale
parameters.relationship: UTM scales distances by about 0.9996 near the zone centre, so areas shrink about 0.08%: roughly 83 m2 on the 103,200 m2 minimum (derived). Keep the factor in Layer 0 and a custom pset; IfcMapConversion.Scale stays 1.0 because it converts units, not grid scale.

parameters.name: Model origin
parameters.relationship: UTM northings near 5.46 million m exceed float32 resolution (about 0.5 m steps, derived), so raw coordinates jitter in WebGL. A site-local origin keeps precision; three-mesh-bvh documents errors for large off-centre geometry.

metrics.name: Unit plausibility
metrics.good: Selected site polygon or tower within +/-2% of 79.2 x 144.8 m after scaling, and tower height inside 244-305 m
metrics.bad: Off by 3x or more, or tower height outside 244-305 m, signalling a unit error
metrics.method: Compare the selected polygon bounds with the brief site after each candidate scale; also test floor-to-floor against an editable 2.5-6 m preset (no source; typical values belong to the program and structure packets)
metrics.basis: Brief gives approximate size; the 2% tolerance and the floor-to-floor preset are team assumptions

metrics.name: True-north error (independent street-edge check)
metrics.good: <= 0.25 deg between the site's street-facing edges and the nearest parcel-derived street bearing (44.7 or 134.7 deg from true north) after the chosen rotation
metrics.method: After the confirmed north type is applied, compute true bearings of the site's edges and compare with the parcel-derived axes; also report the arrow-to-street angle (about 44.7 or 45.3 deg for a true or UTM-grid arrow, about 29.3 or 60.7 deg for a magnetic arrow, derived). Result is 'unchecked' if the site is not on the CBD grid
metrics.basis: Team presets. r1 compared the arrow-converted bearing with a 'confirmed true north' usually taken from the same arrow, which is circular. Parcel edges scatter about 0.1-0.2 deg, so 0.25 deg is resolvable. Derived: 1 deg moves a 300 m tower's shadow tip about 17 m at winter-solstice noon (965 m shadow) and 6 m at equinox noon; 0.25 deg gives about 1.5-4 m

metrics.name: North type confirmed
metrics.good: User has confirmed one of the four north types and the matching correction (declination, convergence or street-grid angle) is applied
metrics.method: Check the required georeference field before releasing the true-north vector
metrics.basis: Team rule; the brief gives no north type

metrics.name: Georeference level (LoGeoRef)
metrics.good: 50: IfcMapConversion (Scale 1.0) plus IfcProjectedCRS (EPSG:3157 and vertical datum)
metrics.bad: 20 or lower: single latitude/longitude, no rotation
metrics.method: Inspect the IFC attributes present; emit IfcMapConversion on export
metrics.basis: Level definitions from the City2BIM wiki; the target level is a team choice

metrics.name: Site position agreement with City reference data
metrics.good: <= 0.3 m after the selected datum shift
metrics.bad: > 1.0 m, which suggests a datum, unit or CRS mix-up
metrics.method: Distance between placed site corners and nearest City parcel vertices in the same portal frame (v1); against LiDAR 2022 building edges once the COPC pipeline exists (roadmap)
metrics.basis: Editable team presets. r1 used 1.0 and 2.0 m, the EPSG 1946 and 1842 accuracies, so its good limit equalled the transformation's own accuracy and could not separate a correct pipeline from a broken one (dropping the rotations alone errs about 0.9 m, derived); parcels are 'not as precise' in places

metrics.name: Transform unit test against PROJ
metrics.good: <= 0.01 m at three site points (two corners and centre) for each datum option versus PROJ
metrics.method: Run proj4js and PROJ for EPSG:3157 to EPSG:4326 (null shift and EPSG 1946) and compare in CI
metrics.basis: Team preset; guards against the radian/arc-second and sign errors in the epsg.io string

metrics.name: Z0 agreement with City LiDAR ground
metrics.good: <= 1.0 m between confirmed Z0 and LiDAR ground at the entrance
metrics.bad: > 3.0 m, which suggests a datum or Z0 error
metrics.method: Sample LiDAR 2022 ground class at the site entrance and compare with the stated geodetic Z0
metrics.basis: Editable presets; LiDAR vertical accuracy 0.081 m at 95%, so metre-scale gaps are datum or Z0 errors, not noise

visualization: Plan view with a four-way north diagram in plain language: true, magnetic, projection (UTM) grid and street-grid north, plus the plan's own arrow, each labelled with its angle from true north
Site outline over City parcel polygons with a distance heat-line and the two street axes (44.7 and 134.7 deg) drawn as dashed lines
Unit-detection card listing candidate scales, and a LoGeoRef 10-50 badge with a checklist of IFC attributes present
Z0 card: local Z0, geodetic elevation and datum beside a LiDAR ground profile at the entrance
modules.method: 1) Units: rhino3dm ModelUnitSystem, IFC IfcUnitAssignment, glTF metres, OBJ ask. 2) Scale check on the selected site polygon or tower, not the whole file: candidates (1, 0.001, 0.01, 0.3048, 0.0254) against 79.2 x 144.8 m within 2%, plus tower-height and floor-to-floor plausibility; the user confirms. 3) CRS: register EPSG:3157 in proj4js with rotations in arc-seconds and position-vector sign (+towgs84=-0.991,1.9072,0.5129,0.025790,0.009650,0.011660,0) or a null shift, chosen by the LiDAR frame test; unit-test against PROJ. 4) Z0: default from City LiDAR ground at the entrance, user confirms; store CGVD28GVRD or CGVD2013. 5) North: the user picks one of four plain-language types; arrow bearing from two clicks; WMM declination, grid convergence (about 0.09 deg), street-grid bearing from parcels (default 44.7/134.7); independent street-edge check. 6) Emit IfcMapConversion (Scale 1.0, OrthogonalHeight = Z0) and IfcProjectedCRS; store float64, render relative to the origin.
modules.human_judgment: Confirming which north the site plan's arrow shows (true, magnetic, UTM grid or street-grid/plan), choosing site origin, entrance level and Z0, and deciding whether to align the model to the street grid.
modules.limits: The organiser's arrow type, vertical datum and the datum name behind footprint 'geodetic' heights are unknown; confirm with the organiser. Whether portal lon/lat is NAD83(CSRS) relabelled as WGS84 is untested. Declination comes from our own WMM evaluation, not checked against NOAA's calculator. The street-grid bearing is derived from one 700 m sample. Georeferencing a hypothetical block is a convention, not a survey.

modules.name: Storey schedule, volume slicing, semantic labelling and Layer 0 assembly
modules.design_question: How do massing volumes and detailed models become per-storey floor plates, voids and confirmed program tags, with evidence, confidence and an area cross-check, ending in a complete Layer 0?
modules.effort: M: core Path A (storey schedule UI, slicing, has_floor voids, manual tagging, area/FSR table) about 3.5 person-days; v1: detailed-model Path B 1.5, rules, LLM stage, review queue and overlap/gap checks about 5 more (team estimate)
inputs: Layer0Checked from P14-M05: closed ProgramVolumes, georeference, site, frontage and access points, trust levels
User storey schedule: ground-floor elevation (Z0), floor-to-floor height per program band, below-grade levels, podium and tower assignment, and per-volume floors-present list (default all levels)
Property bag per object (layer path, name, user strings, IFC class and psets)
Geometry summary (bounding box, area, normals, Z extents)
Layer 0 tag vocabulary; FSR denominator choice; optional designer examples for few-shot prompts
outputs: Level table {name, elevation, floor-to-floor, below_grade, origin: schedule | imported | detected}
FloorPlate records {volume_id, level_id, tag, has_floor, gross_area, outline polygon}
Per-level, per-tag area table: gross_area, floored_area, void_area, counted_fsr_area, counts_to_employment_FSR, fsr_exclusion_reason, with the FSR denominator and its source
Plate-sum area cross-check per volume; ProposedTag list {object_id, tag, confidence, evidence[], origin rule|AI} and review queue (v1)
Layer0Complete: accepted tags with tag_origin and confidence; result card names the path that ran

parameters.name: Storey schedule (floor-to-floor per program band)
parameters.relationship: A taller floor-to-floor in a band gives fewer plates within a fixed tower height and so less floor area; the schedule, not the mesh, sets storey count for massing. Typical values belong to the structure and program packets and are not sourced here.

parameters.name: Slicing method (mid-height slice vs band intersection)
parameters.relationship: A slice at mid-storey height gives plate area exactly for prismatic volumes but only approximates tapered or curved ones; intersecting each slab band and dividing volume by floor-to-floor tracks the taper. manifold-3d exposes slice(height) and volume().

parameters.name: Voids, atria and mezzanines (has_floor)
parameters.relationship: A per-volume floors-present list and FloorPlate.has_floor stop atria, double-height lobbies and sky gardens counting as floor. Only floored plates add to gross and counted FSR area; void area is listed apart. A mezzanine becomes a PARTIAL storey.

parameters.name: Zero-level definition (entrance floor)
parameters.relationship: Which level is ground changes storey numbering and tower height; CTBUH uses the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance, and below-grade levels get negative elevations.

parameters.name: Floor-detection Z tolerance and path gate (Path B, v1)
parameters.relationship: For detailed models only: a wider tolerance merges mezzanines and double-height floors, a narrower one splits sloped slabs. A single extrusion has only top and bottom faces, so detection needs at least 3 horizontal-face clusters; counting follows CTBUH.

parameters.name: Rule layer (IFC class and layer-name dictionary)
parameters.relationship: Deterministic rules explain themselves and cover well-labelled IFC/Revit exports; coverage falls for .3dm and OBJ with ad-hoc layer names, which is where the AI step is needed.

parameters.name: AI model and structured-output schema
parameters.relationship: A schema-constrained reply guarantees parseable tags with evidence strings, not correct ones. The API cannot enforce numeric min/max (SDK helpers validate locally), and refusals or truncation can break the schema, so confidence gating and human confirmation are required.

parameters.name: Auto-accept confidence threshold
parameters.relationship: A higher threshold gives fewer wrong auto-tags but more manual confirmations; items below it go to the review queue. Values are team assumptions until calibrated on a labelled set.

parameters.name: Hosted-API data handling
parameters.relationship: Sending names and layer text to a hosted model exposes project information. Anthropic states API inputs and outputs are deleted within 30 days by default, with zero retention only by agreement; the tool is opt-in per project with a rules-only mode.

metrics.name: Plate-sum area cross-check
metrics.good: <= 0.5% difference between the sum of floored plate area x floor-to-floor and the volume's own volume (void volume excluded)
metrics.method: Compare manifold volume of each ProgramVolume with the sum over its FloorPlates
metrics.basis: Team presets; prismatic volumes should agree to rounding, tapered ones show the mid-height slice error

metrics.name: Void flag consistency
metrics.good: 0 plates with has_floor = false counted in gross or FSR area; void share reported per volume
metrics.method: Scan the area table for void plates with non-zero counted area; report void area divided by gross volume footprint area
metrics.basis: Team rule; void share is design intent and is reported, not judged

metrics.name: Storey count error vs author's count
metrics.method: Scheduled or detected storeys (CTBUH counting) minus the count the author states
metrics.basis: Counting rule from CTBUH; thresholds are team assumptions (off by one shown amber)

metrics.name: Program overlap volume (v1)
metrics.good: <= 0.1% of total program volume
metrics.method: Mesh Boolean intersection of volumes within each storey, run after tags are confirmed
metrics.basis: Team assumption (moved from P14-M05 stage B in r2)

metrics.name: Tag precision on a gold set (v1)
metrics.good: >= 95% for auto-accepted tags
metrics.method: Hold-out set of team-labelled models (including VTC test massings)
metrics.basis: No literature benchmark retrieved; editable preset

metrics.name: Tag coverage after confirmation
metrics.good: 100% of enclosed floored area tagged and confirmed
metrics.method: Tagged plate area divided by total floored plate area
metrics.basis: Team rule

metrics.name: Human override rate (v1)
metrics.good: <= 10% of AI tags changed by the user
metrics.method: Changed tags divided by AI-proposed tags per project
metrics.basis: Team assumption; signals prompt or dictionary quality

visualization: 3D view: each ProgramVolume cut by translucent storey planes with elevation ticks and labels; plates coloured by tag, opacity or hatch showing confidence; void plates (has_floor = false) cross-hatched
Level x tag area table with gross, floored, void and counted columns, employment-flagged tags outlined, and a plate-sum error badge per volume (green <= 0.5%, red > 2%)
Review table sorted by lowest confidence; click zooms to the object with an evidence popover (for example 'layer L12_OFFICE matched rule R3')
modules.method: Path A (massing, default): the user enters a storey schedule (Z0, floor-to-floor per program band, below-grade levels) and, per volume, which levels have floors (default all). Each closed ProgramVolume is cut by manifold-3d (slice, volume) at schedule elevations into FloorPlate records; plate areas times heights are compared with the volume. Void plates are kept with has_floor = false and excluded from gross and FSR area. Path B (v1, detailed IFC/Revit): read IfcBuildingStorey or levels, else cluster slab Z values when at least 3 clusters exist. Tagging: stage 1 rules (IFC class, Revit category, layer tokens); stage 2 stacked-footprint cores; stage 3 (v1) LLM for unresolved items from names and layers only; stage 4 human review. After tags are confirmed, overlap and gap checks (v1) and tag coverage run, and M04 emits Layer0Complete. AI calls log model id, prompt hash and output for P14-M06.
modules.human_judgment: The storey schedule, the entrance zero level, which levels of a volume have floors and every tag are the designer's decisions; rules and AI only propose. Ambiguous uses (hotel lobby versus public space, amenity versus residential) remain a judgement.
modules.limits: Slicing needs closed manifold volumes and horizontal storey bands; split levels beyond PARTIAL mezzanines are not handled in v1. No labelling benchmark was retrieved, so thresholds stay team assumptions. The 3-cluster gate is our assumption. LLM output varies with model version, and hosted use raises confidentiality questions for competition entries. manifold-3d JS slice(height), volume() and CrossSection.area() are confirmed in its type file.

modules.name: Geometry health and brief precheck
modules.design_question: Is the imported geometry closed, correctly scaled, inside plausible brief limits and clear of protected view cones before slicing? What fails, where, and under which height convention?
modules.effort: S-M: core stage A (closed volumes, normals, scale, envelope, three height conventions) about 2 person-days; v1: protected-view cone check about 0.5 (team estimate). Overlap and gap checks moved to P14-M04.
inputs: Layer0Georef from P14-M03 (meshes, units, georeference, site boundary, frontage, access points)
Import report from P14-M02
Optional (v1, from P14-M08): ViewCone polygons and hand-entered limit elevations
outputs: Layer0Checked
Health report: severity, location and suggested fix per rule
Trust level per downstream input (pass / warn / block)
Brief precheck table: tower height under three conventions, site size, view-cone status (v1)
Auto-fix actions (weld, flip normals, rescale)

parameters.name: Weld tolerance
parameters.relationship: Larger tolerance closes small gaps but collapses thin features; too small leaves open edges that make volume and floor area wrong.

parameters.name: Closed-volume requirement by class
parameters.relationship: ProgramVolumes must be closed for volume and area to be valid; context surfaces and site plates may stay open without affecting shadow or wind results.

parameters.name: Brief envelope (height 244-305 m, site 79.2 x 144.8 m)
parameters.relationship: Heights or site sizes outside the envelope usually signal unit or zero-level mistakes. The brief allows justified breaches, so flags warn rather than block.

parameters.name: Height measurement convention
parameters.relationship: One tower reads different heights: CTBUH entrance to architectural top, geodetic top elevation (Z0 plus height), or height above the City by-law base surface (definition not read). Showing all three makes the 244-305 m check state its convention.

parameters.name: Protected-view cone check (v1)
parameters.relationship: A tower footprint touching a cone polygon whose hand-entered limit lies below the geodetic top (Z0 plus height) is flagged; with no limit entered the result is 'unchecked'. The dataset gives polygons only, so limits come from the by-laws.

parameters.name: Analysis triangle budget
parameters.relationship: More triangles improve accuracy but slow BVH queries; three-mesh-bvh quotes 500 rays at 60 fps on an 80,000-polygon model as a reference scale.

metrics.name: Closed-manifold share of ProgramVolumes
metrics.bad: Any open volume feeding area or volume metrics
metrics.method: Edge-use count (each edge shared by exactly two faces); Brep.IsSolid and IsManifold for .3dm
metrics.basis: Team rule; rhino3dm binds IsSolid and IsManifold

metrics.name: Tower height (shown under three conventions)
metrics.good: 244-305 m under the active convention (default: CTBUH entrance to architectural top, excluding antennas and signage)
metrics.bad: Outside the range (warn; a justified breach may be rewarded)
metrics.method: CTBUH: Z of architectural top minus Z of the lowest significant open-air entrance floor; geodetic: Z0 plus that height; by-law base-surface height only when the user enters it
metrics.basis: UNVERIFIED: the 244-305 m range comes from the project packet; the brief PDF was not opened (P14-S54 opened=false; the public page still links the brief to '#' on 21 Oct 2026) and its measurement convention is unknown. The r1 'verified' and 'false_assumption_corrected' labels were both wrong for this metric (FALSE ASSUMPTION flags r1 and r2). The CTBUH rule itself is sourced

metrics.name: Site bounding-box match
metrics.good: Within 2% of 79.2 x 144.8 m
metrics.method: Compare site polygon bounds with the brief
metrics.basis: Brief gives approximate size; tolerances are team assumptions

metrics.name: View-cone check status (v1)
metrics.good: Every cone polygon touching the site has a limit with source and status, and the tower's geodetic top is at or below it
metrics.bad: A touching cone with no limit ('unchecked'), or the top above the limit
metrics.method: 2D intersection of the site footprint with the 24 cones from P14-M08, then comparison of Z0 plus tower height with the entered limit
metrics.basis: Team logic; the dataset has no height fields and the by-laws are authoritative, so limits stay hand-entered

visualization: 3D overlay: open edges red lines, flipped faces magenta, out-of-envelope parts hatched, view-cone breach in orange
Checklist of pass/warn/block rules, each linked to its source clause (for example 'VTC brief: 244-305 m')
Height card: three bars (CTBUH, geodetic, by-law base) against the 244-305 m band
Trust badge on each downstream node input
modules.method: Run in a worker, before slicing. (1) Edge-use histogram: every edge shared by exactly two faces means closed and manifold; IsSolid/IsManifold for .3dm B-reps. (2) Signed volume sign to detect inverted normals. (3) Degenerate and duplicate faces. (4) Unit sanity and brief envelope, with height reported under three conventions (CTBUH from the user-confirmed entrance floor to the architectural top, geodetic top, City base surface when entered). (5) v1: intersect the site footprint with P14-M08's ViewCone polygons and compare the geodetic top with hand-entered limits. Each rule returns severity, location and fix. 'Block' stops dependent modules; 'warn' lets them run with a provisional label shown on every result card. Overlap, gap and tag-coverage checks run in P14-M04 after slicing, which keeps the graph acyclic.
modules.human_judgment: Deciding whether an open volume is a modelling error or design intent, whether an out-of-envelope result is a justified breach, and which view-cone limits to enter from the by-laws.
modules.limits: Mesh checks cannot prove design intent; open context meshes are legitimate. The brief says its documents are academic and the jury may reward justified breaches, so envelope flags are warnings. The CTBUH rule needs the user to identify the lowest significant entrance. The brief's own height convention and the by-law base-surface definition were not read.

modules.name: Design-state versioning, provenance, visibility and anonymised export
modules.design_question: How are design states, assumptions and module results stored, shared and anonymised so any result can be reproduced, compared, forked and traced to sources, including flagged false assumptions that stay visible?
modules.effort: M: snapshots, hashing, schema pinning and result cards about 4 person-days (minimal provenance fields ship in P14-M01 for core); visibility and anonymised export about 2; diff view about 4; fork and merge about 5 (team estimate)
inputs: Layer0Complete and geometry blobs; optional ContextLayer hash from P14-M08
Module graph configuration (nodes on/off, parameter values, assumption overrides)
Module outputs and source ids
Author and timestamp
Anonymise flag and pseudonym; visibility choice (private, team, public)
outputs: Snapshot ids (content hash) with parent links and pinned schema_version
Diff {objects added/removed/changed, tag changes, parameter changes}
Provenance graph of Entity, Activity and Agent, including schema migrations
Result cards: 'computed from snapshot X, schema vS, module vY, parameters Z'
Append-only assumption log including FALSE ASSUMPTION flags
Anonymised export package plus a residual-identifier scan report; visibility record per state and fork

parameters.name: Snapshot granularity (per edit / per module run / manual commit)
parameters.relationship: Finer snapshots give exact undo and reproducibility but multiply storage and noise; manual commits are cheap but results may refer to uncommitted state, so every result card must pin a snapshot.

parameters.name: Hashing and canonical form
parameters.relationship: Content hashes deduplicate identical states and expose silent changes. Speckle's older graph used content identity; 2026.9 keys objects by applicationId, so Layer 0 computes its own SHA-256. Unsorted JSON keys or unrounded floats break hashes unless canonicalised.

parameters.name: Storage backend (Speckle / git-in-browser / custom)
parameters.relationship: Speckle brings versions, viewer and connectors, but its format changed at 2026.9 and the Free plan keeps 100 versions with 30-day history. Browser git is free but needs a CORS proxy for clone and push and can reorder writes.

parameters.name: Module version pinning
parameters.relationship: Forked modules may change thresholds. Without module version and threshold sources stored on each result, a diff of metrics cannot tell a design change from a rule change.

parameters.name: Assumption log retention
parameters.relationship: Entries move team assumption to verified or FALSE ASSUMPTION but are never deleted; deletion would hide why earlier results changed. This is a project requirement, not an external standard.

parameters.name: Merge model (snapshot fork vs real-time sync)
parameters.relationship: Snapshot fork and three-way merge matches GitHub-like community forking and is simpler; real-time CRDT sync merges concurrent edits automatically but needs per-object conflict rules and is deferred.

parameters.name: Anonymised export (identifier stripping)
parameters.relationship: VTC entries are evaluated anonymously. The IFC header FILE_NAME carries author and organization, IfcOwnerHistory (optional in IFC4) names people and applications, and Speckle versions carry an author; the export blanks or pseudonymises each and the ledger keeps real identity locally.

parameters.name: Visibility and sharing default
parameters.relationship: Design states are private by default; team and public are opt-in. The VTC terms bar visual materials 'previously published' (clause 4.1, read via a page tool), so public forks of design-state geometry stay blocked until 30 Nov 2026 unless the owner opts in. Module code and thresholds are shared separately. Speckle Free public links stop after 30 days.

parameters.name: Schema version in replay
parameters.relationship: Replays migrate stored states to the current schema_version before comparing hashes and log the migration as a PROV Activity; otherwise a schema change is indistinguishable from a design change or a rule change.

metrics.name: Reproducibility
metrics.good: 100% of deterministic results regenerate with an identical output hash from snapshot plus module version, after migration to the current schema
metrics.method: Nightly replay of stored result cards
metrics.basis: Course requirement to show work; threshold is a team rule

metrics.name: Provenance completeness
metrics.good: 100% of displayed numbers link to a source id and snapshot, or carry a 'team assumption' badge
metrics.bad: Any unsourced number without a badge
metrics.method: Scan result cards for missing source_ids
metrics.basis: Course requirement (every result cites its source)

metrics.name: UI latency while snapshotting or diffing (INP p75)
metrics.method: Run hashing and diff in workers; measure event timing for clicks and key presses
metrics.basis: web.dev INP thresholds

metrics.name: Residual identifiers in anonymised export
metrics.good: 0 found in IFC header and OwnerHistory, GLB asset and extras, Speckle author, PROV agents, file paths and image EXIF
metrics.method: Automated scan of every exported file after pseudonymisation
metrics.basis: Team rule derived from the VTC anonymity statement and terms clause 5.1

metrics.name: Visibility default audit
metrics.good: 100% of new design states and forks created private; 0 public design-state forks before the submission deadline without an owner opt-in
metrics.bad: >= 1 public state or fork without opt-in
metrics.method: Automated check of the visibility record on every snapshot and fork
metrics.basis: Team rule from VTC terms 4.1 (interpretation unconfirmed)

visualization: Commit graph (git-style DAG) coloured by author and fork, with a lock icon on private states
Two-snapshot diff: 3D ghost overlay (added green, removed red, moved amber) with a table of parameter and metric deltas
Result card chain source > snapshot > schema > module version > metric, drawn with PROV-style arrows; FALSE ASSUMPTION entries in the special colour on the timeline
Anonymise dialog listing each scrubbed field before and after, with a pass/fail scan badge
modules.method: Canonicalise Layer 0 JSON (sorted keys, floats rounded to 1e-6 m) and hash geometry blobs (SHA-256). A snapshot is a Merkle-style manifest {layer0_hash, schema_version, geometry_hashes, context_layer_hash, graph_config_hash, assumptions_hash, parent_ids, author, time, visibility}. Diff by object id (added, removed, then attribute diffs). Results are PROV-O: a result Entity wasGeneratedBy a module-run Activity that used the snapshot and sources, wasAttributedTo an Agent; replay migrates old snapshots first and logs it as an Activity. Forks copy manifest pointers; merge is three-way with conflicts listed for a human. New states are private; a public geometry fork needs an owner opt-in and is blocked before 30 Nov 2026 by default. Anonymised export blanks FILE_NAME author and organization, omits OwnerHistory, pseudonymises Speckle author, PROV agents and file paths, then scans for residual identifiers.
modules.human_judgment: When to commit, how to name a design state, resolving merge conflicts, deciding when an assumption has been disproved and must be flagged, whether an export is safe to share, and whether sharing a state breaches the competition's publication rule.
modules.limits: Hash reproducibility holds only for deterministic modules; WASM or browser floating-point differences and LLM steps (P14-M04) break bit-exactness, so those results store the produced output. Speckle Free keeps 100 versions and 30 days. Whether private or team sharing counts as 'previously published' is unconfirmed. VTC boards are JPEG images (clause 4.8), so board metadata belongs to PRES; this scrubber covers shared model files and forks.

modules.name: Browser geometry kernel and performance budget
modules.design_question: Which in-browser and optional server geometry stack handles tower-scale models fast enough for interactive evaluation, and when must work move to a worker, a server or Rhino.Compute?
modules.effort: S-M: core shell, workers and float64 store about 1.5 person-days; performance HUD about 1 (v1); OpenCascade and Compute integration roadmap (team estimate)
inputs: Mesh buffers and compute requests passed by callers (M02, M04, M05 and other packets' modules); M07 is a runtime service with no data ports, so it sits outside the module DAG
Device capability, hosting headers and file size
outputs: Render mesh with LOD and analysis mesh with BVH
Section polylines and Boolean results
Performance report (ms, MB per node)
Offload-recommended flag per task

parameters.name: Tessellation tolerance and LOD
parameters.relationship: Coarser meshes speed ray casting for sun and view modules but understate curved-facade area; three-mesh-bvh's 500 rays at 60 fps on 80,000 polygons is a reference scale for analysis meshes.

parameters.name: Compute location (main thread / worker / server / Rhino.Compute)
parameters.relationship: Main-thread work over 50 ms hurts responsiveness; workers keep the canvas interactive. Rhino.Compute adds exact Rhino geometry but needs Rhino 8 for Windows; McNeel says core-hour billing (USD 0.10 per core-hour) is incompatible with Educational licences; workstation use is unaddressed.

parameters.name: Kernel choice (mesh vs B-rep vs rhino3dm)
parameters.relationship: Mesh kernels (three.js, three-mesh-bvh, manifold) are small and fast but approximate. OCCT-based opencascade.js gives exact B-rep and STEP but its WASM is large; rhino3dm reads Rhino data but has no Brep meshing or tessellation.

parameters.name: Numeric precision (float64 store, origin-relative render)
parameters.relationship: UTM northings near 5.46 million m exceed float32's 0.5 m resolution (derived); subtracting a site origin before upload keeps sub-millimetre precision at tower scale.

parameters.name: Memory ceiling and streaming
parameters.relationship: In practice each WASM module's declared maximum memory, not a browser-wide 4 GiB, is the limit, to be read per module. Memory64 is stable in Chrome and Firefox but only a Safari preview. City LiDAR tiles reach 2.74 GB zipped, so COPC range requests are used.

parameters.name: Hosting and cross-origin isolation
parameters.relationship: The multithreaded web-ifc build needs SharedArrayBuffer, which needs COOP and COEP headers; static hosts such as GitHub Pages cannot set them. A service-worker shim reloads once on first visit, or the single-thread build loads, trading import speed for simple hosting.

parameters.name: Distribution licences of bundled WASM
parameters.relationship: opencascade.js is LGPL-2.1: a statically linked bundle needs source and relinking terms, while a separately fetched, replaceable WASM file fits LGPL section 6(b). LibreDWG is GPL-3.0 and stays server-side. The project's own licence is a team decision.

metrics.name: Input latency (INP, p75)
metrics.method: PerformanceObserver event timing for clicks and key presses during imports; INP does not observe drags or scrolling, so slider drags are covered by the frame-time metric
metrics.basis: web.dev INP thresholds

metrics.name: Frame work per frame
metrics.good: <= 10 ms (16 ms budget at 60 fps)
metrics.method: Render stats and performance marks while orbiting the model
metrics.basis: RAIL: produce frames in 10 ms because the browser needs about 6 ms. Source verified, but RAIL targets mobile web pages; applying it to a desktop WASM canvas is our assumption

metrics.name: Task chunk length
metrics.good: <= 50 ms chunks
metrics.method: Long Task observer
metrics.basis: RAIL: idle work in 50 ms chunks, respond within 100 ms (mobile page-load model; applicability assumed)

metrics.name: Canvas shell interactive (no model loaded)
metrics.good: <= 5 s on mid-range mobile over slow 3G; later loads < 2 s
metrics.method: Lighthouse; lazy-load rhino3dm, web-ifc and OCCT WASM after the shell
metrics.basis: RAIL load target for mobile; a desktop-first design tool may relax it (assumption)

metrics.name: Peak WASM heap
metrics.good: <= 50% of the module's declared maximum memory
metrics.method: Sample memory.buffer.byteLength against the module's declared maximum, per module and per browser (Safari first)
metrics.basis: Team presets. r1 replaced a 4 GiB wasm32 ceiling (general knowledge, unopened; FALSE ASSUMPTION flag) because a module stops at its own maximum

visualization: Performance HUD in the canvas corner (fps, frame ms, long-task count, heap MB and % of declared max) with traffic-light bands from the thresholds (v1)
Per-node timing bar on each canvas node showing parse, mesh, BVH and compute time
Offload banner naming the task and the measured cost when a threshold is crossed
Hosting badge showing crossOriginIsolated true or false and which web-ifc build loaded
modules.method: Parse in a worker (rhino3dm, web-ifc) into a Float64 geometry store, subtract the site origin, and upload Float32 buffers to three.js BufferGeometry. Build an analysis mesh with decimation and a three-mesh-bvh tree. Modules call workers by RPC for ray casts (sun, view), section planes, area and volume. Use manifold-3d for mesh Booleans, slicing and validation; lazy-load opencascade.js (custom build, separate file) only when a module needs exact B-rep or STEP. Check self.crossOriginIsolated at start; load web-ifc-mt only when true. Offload rule: if a task exceeds 100 ms measured, or a file exceeds the tested size, move it to a server worker running IfcOpenShell or rhino3dm.py; use Rhino.Compute only if a licensed server exists. Record timings with PerformanceObserver and memory against each module's declared maximum. CI checks the licence column of every bundled component.
modules.human_judgment: Choosing speed versus accuracy (tessellation, offloading), accepting approximations on curved geometry, and choosing the project licence and host.
modules.limits: The opencascade.js repo page shows an OCCT 7.6.2 badge and no listed releases, so maintenance is unclear and its bundle is large unless custom-built (unverified). McNeel calls rhino3dm.wasm fairly large. Benchmarks quoted are on an Apple M1 and will not match student laptops. Rhino.Compute needs Windows and Rhino 8; whether workstation use is allowed for students is unverified.

modules.name: City of Vancouver context ingest, view cones and viewpoints
modules.design_question: What surrounding buildings, terrain and protected views can City open data supply, how current and accurate are they, and what must be added by hand, such as approved towers?
modules.effort: S-M: Queen Elizabeth Park cones, viewpoint, footprints and parcels about 4.5 person-days; LiDAR to COPC pipeline about 1 week, roadmap (team estimate). Skip if the organiser's 3D model already includes context.
inputs: Site anchor (longitude/latitude or EPSG:3157 easting/northing picked on a map) and context radius
Organiser's context model, if provided
Selected City datasets
User-entered viewpoints and view-limit elevations (with source and status)
Organiser's reference photo heights (five labelled towers)
outputs: ContextLayer in EPSG:3157 with geodetic heights (the local frame comes from P14-M03's matrix)
ContextBuilding list {footprint, base_elev, top_elev, parts, source dataset, year, licence}
Terrain surface
ViewCone records {polygon, viewpoint_xyz, limit_elevation_m, limit_source, limit_status} for the 24 polygons
Viewpoint objects (Queen Elizabeth Park skyline, mid-city) shared with PRES
Parcel polygons, rapid transit lines, street-grid bearing from parcel edges and LiDAR ground at the anchor (optional inputs to P14-M03)
Context currency report; manual-add queue for approved towers

parameters.name: Context radius
parameters.relationship: A larger radius adds distant towers that cast long shadows or channel wind but increases triangles and download. The radius needed as a function of tower height is not sourced here and belongs to the CLIM packets.

parameters.name: Height source (footprints 2009 / LiDAR 2022 / organiser model / OSM and Overture)
parameters.relationship: Footprints derive from 2009 LiDAR and are not updated, so towers built since are missing. LiDAR 2022 (about 49 points/m2, 0.081 m vertical accuracy at 95%) catches them but needs processing; Overture and OSM add newer footprints under ODbL.

parameters.name: Part handling (one building id, several polygons)
parameters.relationship: A building appears as stacked polygons with different base and top elevations. Extruding each from baseelev_m to topelev_m reproduces podium plus tower; maxht_m is the maximum over all parts of the building, so use it only for building-level summaries.

parameters.name: Coordinate frame and vertical datum of City data
parameters.relationship: LiDAR 2022 is NAD83(CSRS) UTM 10 with CGVD28GVRD heights; footprint heights are 'geodetic' without a named datum, and parcel and footprint pages state no CRS. Portal lon/lat may be relabelled NAD83(CSRS) or true WGS84, about 1.3 m apart here; test against LiDAR.

parameters.name: Manual additions (approved, unbuilt towers)
parameters.relationship: The brief says context includes approved towers; no open dataset of approved massing was found. The tallest 2009 footprint within 2.5 km of the CBD is 208.6 m (maxht_m, derived), so nothing in the 244-305 m class is present; omitting approved towers under-predicts shadow and wind interaction.

parameters.name: Protected view cones and limit elevations (24 polygons)
parameters.relationship: Building heights inside cones are limited, but the dataset gives polygons only, no height fields. The check in P14-M05 intersects the tower footprint with each polygon and compares its geodetic top with a hand-entered limit; with no limit the result is 'unchecked'.

parameters.name: Viewpoints (Queen Elizabeth Park skyline, mid-city)
parameters.relationship: The brief asks for a Queen Elizabeth Park skyline view and a mid-city view. The dataset has four Queen Elizabeth Park cones (3.2.1-3.2.4) but no viewpoint coordinates; the organiser's reference photo shows the framing and labels five tower heights. Position and direction are entered as Viewpoint objects.

parameters.name: Licence and attribution
parameters.relationship: City data is under Open Government Licence - Vancouver; OSM-derived layers are ODbL (share-alike). The tool must show attribution and keep ODbL layers separable.

metrics.name: Agreement with organiser reference heights
metrics.good: <= 5% difference for each of the five labelled towers (141-201 m)
metrics.bad: > 10% for any, or a labelled tower missing
metrics.method: Compare footprint or LiDAR heights at each tower's position with the labels in the organiser's Queen Elizabeth Park photo
metrics.basis: Team presets. Indicative r2 check by position only (the dataset has no names): the footprint at Living Shangri-La's location has parts of 188.6 and 192.9 m and maxht_m 208.6 m against 201 m; at Harbour Centre a 135.3 m part and maxht_m 160.2 m against 147 m

metrics.good: Every cone polygon touching the site has a hand-entered limit elevation with source and status
metrics.bad: A touching cone with no limit ('unchecked')

visualization: Context massing extruded from City data, coloured by data year (cool recent, warm old), with a ring at the chosen radius
View-cone polygons as translucent ground wedges with labels and a pass/unchecked/fail chip; LiDAR-derived terrain as hillshade
Viewpoint markers with a camera frustum for the Queen Elizabeth Park and mid-city views, with the organiser's five labelled towers as height ticks

modules.method: Fetch GeoJSON from the City open-data API (building-footprints-2009, property-parcel-polygons, view-cones, rapid-transit-lines) within the radius, starting with the four Queen Elizabeth Park cones (3.2.1-3.2.4) and the viewpoint. Check returned coordinates against LiDAR before choosing the datum shift, then reproject with proj4js (EPSG:3157 registered, shift per P14-M03). Group by bldgid; extrude each part from baseelev_m to topelev_m, check topelev_m minus baseelev_m equals hgt_agl, and keep heights geodetic; P14-M03's matrix places them in the local frame. Derive the street-grid bearing from parcel edges and sample ground at the anchor for Z0. Roadmap: convert LiDAR 2022 LAS tiles (up to 2.74 GB zipped) to COPC server-side. The organiser's model takes priority; users add approved towers as boxes tagged 'manual, team assumption'.
modules.human_judgment: Which context matters, adding approved-but-unbuilt towers, entering view-limit elevations from the by-laws, placing the viewpoints, and deciding whether to trust an old dataset over the organiser's model.
modules.limits: Footprints 2009 are generalised and not updated; towers completed since are absent or wrong. The view-cone dataset has polygons only: allowable height surfaces are in by-laws, and the City's view pages and policy PDFs returned HTTP 403. The vertical datum name behind topelev_m is not stated beyond 'geodetic'. The City licence text could not be opened. Matching labelled towers to footprints is by position only.

sources.title: IFC 4.3 spatial structure pages: IfcSpace, IfcSpatialZone, IfcBuildingStorey, IfcBuilding, IfcSite, IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure, IfcAnnotation (GitHub docs)
sources.extract: Re-read 21 Oct 2026. IfcSpace belongs to a storey, or to a site if exterior. IfcSpatialZone (new in IFC4): non-hierarchical, may overlap, own placement and shape; spaces it references use IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure, with the zone as RelatingStructure and spaces as RelatedElements (an 'IFC4 CHANGE' allows IfcSpace there); a zone can itself be referenced by another spatial element. IfcBuildingStorey: aggregated by its building; PARTIAL = partial storey (split-level example); Elevation deprecated in 4.3 (use Pset_BuildingStoreyCommon ElevationOfSSLRelative/FFLRelative). IfcBuilding: COMPLEX/ELEMENT/PARTIAL (building section); ElevationOfRefHeight deprecated in 4.3. IfcSite.RefElevation is the site reference height. IfcAnnotation: points, curves and symbolic information that are not products or spatial structure. IFC4 ADD2 equivalents not read.

sources.title: Transverse Mercator projection (Wikipedia)
sources.extract: Convergence gamma = arctan(tan(lambda) sin(phi)); point scale k0 / sqrt(1 - sin^2 lambda cos^2 phi). Derived r2: at 49.2827 N, 123.1207 W this gives convergence about 0.09 degree and point scale about 0.99960.

sources.title: proj4js (repository, lib/datum.js and lib/datumUtils.js)
sources.extract: Predefines EPSG 4326, 4269, 3857 and WGS84 UTM zones (not 26910 or 3157); custom definitions via proj4.defs; accepts WKT and PROJJSON; licence not named on the page. Code re-read 21 Oct 2026: datum.js multiplies the +towgs84 rotation terms by SEC_TO_RAD (arc-seconds to radians) and datumUtils.js applies position-vector formulas (x' = x - rz*y + ry*z + dx), so radian values pasted as arc-seconds are effectively zero. The nad83 datum entry has towgs84 0,0,0 and there is no NAD83 CSRS entry.

sources.title: IFC 4.3 IfcMapConversion, IfcMapConversionScaled and IfcProjectedCRS (GitHub docs)
sources.extract: IfcMapConversion (new in IFC4): Eastings, Northings, OrthogonalHeight (relative to the vertical datum specified), XAxisAbscissa/XAxisOrdinate for rotation, one Scale on x, y, z 'to convert units' (default 1.0). IfcMapConversionScaled (new in IFC4X3 ADD1) adds FactorX/Y/Z 'to scale coordinates, not units'. IfcProjectedCRS: Name, GeodeticDatum, VerticalDatum (needed for 3D systems when Name does not define it), MapProjection, MapZone, MapUnit.

sources.title: IFC 4.3 property, quantity, classification and root pages (GitHub docs)
sources.extract: Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities: GrossFloorArea, GrossPerimeter, Height, NetFloorArea, NetVolume. IfcPropertySet: user-defined sets must not use the Pset_ prefix. IfcClassification: Source, Edition, EditionDate, Name; a declared classification may be formally published (OmniClass, Uniclass) or locally defined. IfcClassificationReference: Identification, Name, ReferencedSource (lightweight or full classification). IfcRoot: GlobalId; OwnerHistory optional in IFC4. Pset_SpaceCommon page lists IsExternal.

sources.title: ISO 10303-21 (STEP-File) header structure (Wikipedia)
sources.extract: HEADER holds FILE_DESCRIPTION, FILE_NAME and FILE_SCHEMA; FILE_NAME has name, time_stamp, author, organization, preprocessor_version, originating_system, authorization; apart from time_stamp and FILE_SCHEMA fields may be left empty.

sources.title: NOAA NCEI World Magnetic Model
sources.extract: WMM2025 epoch 2025.0, valid until late 2029 (expires 31 Dec 2029); software outputs an uncertainty per component; no declination value for Vancouver was retrieved from NOAA (the online calculator was reported to need a registered API key and was not used).

sources.extract: Inputs and outputs for API users are deleted from the backend within 30 days by default, with exceptions (longer retention you control, agreed terms, Usage Policy enforcement, legal requirements); zero retention only by agreement; page does not state training use.

No rule on AI tools found.

sources.extract: Image viewed 21 Oct 2026: a skyline photograph from Queen Elizabeth Park with five labelled towers: Butterfly 586 ft (179 m), One Wall Centre 491 ft (150 m), Living Shangri-La 659 ft (201 m), Royal Centre 463 ft (141 m), Harbour Centre 482 ft (147 m). No caption, viewpoint coordinates or datum.

sources.title: EPSG:1946 NAD83(CSRS) to WGS 84 (2)
sources.extract: Method Coordinate Frame rotation (EPSG 9607); accuracy 1.0 m; translations -0.991, 1.9072, 0.5129 m; rotations -1.25033E-07, -4.6785E-08, -5.6529E-08 radian (the page's PROJ string shows -0.0257899, -0.0096501, -0.0116599 arc-seconds with +convention=coordinate_frame); scale 0 ppm; an approximation from tfm code 6864 ignoring time-dependent parameters. Derived r2: in position-vector form the rotations are +0.025790, +0.009650, +0.011660 arc-seconds; at the site the rotation terms alone shift a point about 0.9 m (0.75 m east, 0.50 m south) and the full 7-parameter shift differs from a null shift by about 1.3 m.

sources.title: PROJ: Helmert transform
sources.extract: Rotations are in arc seconds; once a rotation is given a convention is required: coordinate_frame (clockwise, EPSG 9607 or 1032) or position_vector (anticlockwise, EPSG 9606 or 1033); negating the rotations converts between them. The PROJ usage page states neither the +towgs84 rotation unit nor its convention.

sources.title: What is openNURBS?
sources.extract: openNURBS is an open-source toolkit for only reading and writing 3DM models; it does not include surface tessellation (meshing), Booleans, SubD to Brep conversion, closest point and intersection, interpolation, or area and mass properties.

sources.title: earcut polygon triangulation
sources.extract: ISC; fast polygon triangulation with holes for WebGL; trades quality for speed and gives no correctness guarantee on invalid input (self-crossing rings, duplicate points can leave overlaps or gaps); a deviation function compares the triangulated area with the input area; output may contain T-junctions.

sources.title: pygeomag (WMM-2025 implementation)
sources.extract: MIT; supports WMM-2025 (default), WMMHR-2025, WMM-2020 and earlier; README example: Seattle 47.6205 N, 122.3493 W, 2025.25, declination 15.0656 degrees. Its WMM_2025.COF coefficient file (epoch 2025.0) was read from the repository on 21 Oct 2026 and evaluated with our own spherical-harmonic code, which reproduces the Seattle value to 4 decimals; the same code gives 15.37 degrees east at 49.2827 N, 123.1207 W for 2026.8 (derived, not checked against NOAA's calculator).

sources.title: Making your website cross-origin isolated using COOP and COEP
sources.extract: Published 2020-04-13, updated 2022-06-21. A page needs Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp on the main document to be cross-origin isolated (self.crossOriginIsolated is true); SharedArrayBuffer requires it on Chrome desktop from version 92.

sources.title: coi-serviceworker
sources.extract: MIT; a service worker that enables cross-origin isolation where you cannot control headers (README example: GitHub Pages); reloads the page once on first load; needs HTTPS or localhost; must be its own file served from your own origin.
