sources.extract: MIT; supports JSON Schema drafts 2019-09 and 2020-12 (plus 06 and 07); Node 18+ and browsers; the project claims it is the fastest validator (own benchmarks).

flags.claim: City of Vancouver building footprints and heights can serve as a current context model
flags.correction: The dataset 'Building footprints 2009' is derived from 2009 LiDAR, 'approximate, best used for comparison' and 'not being updated'. Use LiDAR 2022 (about 49 points/m2) or the organiser's 3D model for current heights.
flags.detail: Data age of footprints is 17 years against 4 years for LiDAR 2022; towers built since 2009 are missing or wrong. r2 check: the tallest footprint within 2.5 km of the CBD is 208.6 m (maxht_m), so nothing in the brief's 244-305 m class is present. See P14-M08.

flags.claim: Rhino can import or export IFC natively, so IFC is a universal route from .3dm
flags.detail: McNeel's Rhino 8 and Rhino 9 import/export indexes list skp, glb/gltf, obj, fbx, dwg and step, but not ifc or rvt. The page notes dialogs show only formats whose plug-ins are enabled, so a plug-in route may exist; not confirmed.

flags.claim: Rhino.Compute can be used by the student team for server-side geometry
flags.detail: Code is MIT but runs on Rhino 8 for Windows. McNeel's page says core-hour billing (USD 0.10 per core per hour) is not compatible with Educational or Commercial licences, cannot be enabled on a team containing licences, and is required on Windows Server-based systems; it does not address workstation use. Whether the course or UBC holds a suitable licence is unknown, so Compute stays optional and not core.

flags.claim: proj4js can transform EPSG:3157 (or 26910) out of the box
flags.correction: proj4js predefines WGS84 UTM zones, not 26910 or 3157; the module must register the NAD83(CSRS) UTM zone 10N definition with proj4.defs, with rotations in arc-seconds (see the r2 FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag on the epsg.io string). Do not use +datum=NAD83, which proj4js defines with towgs84 0,0,0.
flags.detail: r2: the registered definition is still untested against a PROJ reference; the unit test in P14-M03 is the gate.

flags.claim: SketchUp .skp can be read directly with the SketchUp C SDK in an open-source tool
flags.detail: Access needs developer registration and agreement to Trimble API terms; redistribution terms were not read (forum thread only). Recommended route is export to OBJ/GLB/IFC, Speckle connector, or Rhino 8 import then save .3dm.

flags.claim: Revit .rvt can be converted to IFC or meshes through APS Model Derivative at acceptable cost
flags.detail: The supported-translations table and pricing page are script-rendered and could not be read. Free tier has monthly caps (numbers not retrieved); paid tier uses Flex tokens; per-job price came from a search snippet only.

flags.claim: IFC4X3 geometry imports reliably in web-ifc and IfcOpenShell
flags.detail: web-ifc enumerates IFC4X3 in its schema file, but the IfcOpenShell README states extensive geometry support only for IFC2x3 TC1 and IFC4 Add2 TC1. IFC4 ADD2 is the default export and import baseline; IFC4X3 stays optional until a tower round-trip spike (IfcSpace, IfcSpatialZone, IfcMapConversion, tessellated geometry) passes in both libraries.

flags.claim: Speckle object model is stable enough to map Layer 0 to
flags.detail: Speckle 2026.9 replaced the nested object graph with bundles (units per object, no Level object, no proxies); compatibility mode for ACC sync and file uploads ends 1 November 2026, and pre-2026.9 SDKs get a 404 on new versions. The mapping targets the 2026.9 model only, pins the 2026.9 SDK and sits in v1; the relations page does not describe site or building containers, so the hierarchy mapping is open.

flags.claim: Organiser's 'Site plans & 3D model' download is in a format and CRS the tool can read
flags.detail: Re-checked 21 Oct 2026: the brief and model links on the public page still have no real URL and no formats, CRS, vertical datum or north-arrow type are stated. Registration closes 29 Oct and Q&A closes 3 Nov 2026, so a team member must register and obtain the package by 28 Oct, with the Q&A list sent by 31 Oct (list in notes). The organiser's Queen Elizabeth View reference photo (P14-S65) is read. If obtainable, add the model as a named CI fixture.

flags.claim: Higher Buildings Policy (1997) is the governing policy for height and view protection
flags.detail: Both policy PDFs returned HTTP 403 again, as did the City's view pages. r2: the City's Shape Your City page (updated 13 Jul 2026) shows the 1997 policy still under review (draft policies fall 2026-winter 2027, adoption spring 2027), so it is not replaced yet, and says protected views are not being reviewed. The view-cones dataset says the City's by-laws are authoritative.

flags.claim: AI-assisted labelling accuracy thresholds (95% auto-accept precision, 80% floor)
flags.detail: No literature on IFC/BIM element classification accuracy was retrieved. These numbers are editable team assumptions to be measured on a labelled VTC test set.

flags.claim: IFC class definitions used in the Layer 0 mapping (IfcSpace, IfcSpatialZone, IfcMapConversion semantics)
flags.detail: r2 closed the IFC4.3 questions: the zone is the RelatingStructure and its spaces the RelatedElements of IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure (IFC4 change), PARTIAL storeys and building sections exist, and IfcMapConversion.Scale converts units. Still unconfirmed: the IFC4 ADD2 pages (IfcSpatialZone, IfcMapConversion, Elevation attributes) and that mapping massing to IfcSpace is accepted practice. The round-trip spike settles these.

flags.claim: All thresholds with status team_assumption in P14 (completeness, parity, overlap, true-north street-edge check 0.25/1 deg, parcel agreement 0.3/1 m, Z0 agreement 1/3 m, plate-sum error 0.5/2%, memory 50/80% of declared maximum, data age, 100 m tall-building cut-off, floor-to-floor 2.5-6 m, 3-cluster gate, RAIL targets applied to a desktop WASM canvas, etc.)
flags.detail: Shown in the tool as editable presets with the reasoning in each metric's basis; none has a published source for this use. Where an EPSG accuracy or derived geometry motivates a value, the basis says so. r2 reset r1-corrected metrics to this status so the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour marks only the logged claims.

flags.claim: EPSG:26910 (proj4 +datum=NAD83) is the right CRS for City of Vancouver data, and mixing it with WGS84 shifts positions 2-4 m
flags.detail: City LiDAR 2022 is NAD83(CSRS) 4.0.0.BC.1.GVRD, not NAD83 original. proj4js defines its nad83 datum with towgs84 0,0,0, so no shift would ever be applied; epsg.io's EPSG:26910 remarks say it is replaced by NAD83(CSRS) / UTM zone 10N in Canada for accuracy better than 1 m. Evidence: P14-S36, P14-S30, P14-S33, P14-S57.
flags.correction: Project CRS is EPSG:3157 NAD83(CSRS) / UTM 10N. EPSG lists the CSRS-to-WGS84 transformation accuracy as 1.0 m (alternative 2.0 m); EPSG:26910 stays an accepted import alias with a warning. See the r2 flag on how the 3157 definition must be registered.

flags.claim: A local Z = 0 at the entrance floor sidesteps vertical datum mixing
flags.detail: City context heights are geodetic (footprints: baseelev_m and topelev_m 'geodetic'; sample building base 30.7 m, top 219.29 m, height above grade 188.59 m) and LiDAR is CGVD28GVRD; protected-view limits are stated as elevations. A bare local zero cannot be stacked on context or tested against view limits. Evidence: P14-S35, P14-S36, P14-S37.
flags.correction: Z0 geodetic elevation and vertical datum are required georeference fields, defaulted from LiDAR ground at the entrance and confirmed by the user, exported as IfcMapConversion.OrthogonalHeight and IfcProjectedCRS.VerticalDatum. EPSG:3157 itself has no vertical axis (P14-S57).

flags.claim: Speckle keys objects by applicationId (cited to the pre-2026.9 data-schema page)
flags.detail: As cited, wrong: P14-S09 says objects are identified by content hash and applicationId gives stable version tracking, and it covers only versions published before 2026.9. The 2026.9 model pages (P14-S10) key objects by applicationId and do not mention content hashes, so identity depends on the Speckle version.
flags.correction: Store IFC GlobalId, source applicationId, Layer 0 UUID and our own SHA-256 separately; cite P14-S10 for the 2026.9 model and treat P14-S09 as historical.

flags.claim: The meaning of avght_m, maxht_m and the datum of topelev_m in Building footprints 2009 is undocumented
flags.detail: The dataset page documents the fields: baseelev_m and topelev_m are the lowest and highest elevations (geodetic), hgt_agl is essentially topelev minus baseelev, avght_m the average element height, maxht_m and minht_m the max and min over all elements sharing a BLDGID, base_m the base elevation of all elements sharing a BLDGID. Sample building 149845 fits. The page names no vertical datum beyond 'geodetic'.
flags.correction: Field meanings moved to resolved (use maxht_m only for building-level summaries); the name of the vertical datum behind topelev_m stays unresolved.

flags.claim: web-ifc benchmark: 29-70 MB files open in 0.45-1.2 s and mesh in 4.6-7.6 s
flags.detail: This picked a subset. In the same table 47 MB executed in 0.52 s, 55 MB in 2.05 s and 70 MB in 5.5 s while 30 MB took 5.3 s and 34 MB took 7.6 s; open times for 26-70 MB range 0.17-1.16 s. Time does not scale with size, and the M1 listed free RAM of about 137 (units not stated). Evidence: P14-S08.
flags.correction: Quote the full range (open 0.17-1.16 s, execute 0.52-7.6 s for 26-70 MB) and set thresholds from our own measurement of a VTC-sized model on a mid-range Windows laptop.

flags.claim: A 1 degree true-north error moves a shadow tip about 1.7 m, which justifies a 0.5 degree target
flags.detail: The geometry is right but the 100 m shadow was the wrong scale. Derived at latitude 49.29 N: noon altitude at winter solstice = 90 - 49.29 - 23.44 = 17.3 degrees, so a 300 m tower casts about 965 m and 1 degree moves the tip about 17 m; at equinox noon the shadow is about 349 m and the shift about 6 m (244-305 m towers: about 5-6 m equinox, 14-17 m solstice).
flags.correction: Tolerance restated as good <= 0.25 degree, bad >= 1 degree (team assumption that depends on the CLIM packets).

flags.claim: The wasm32 4 GiB memory ceiling is the browser limit for imports
flags.detail: The 4 GiB figure was general knowledge, not an opened page, and as a 'bad' threshold it is unreachable because each module stops at its own declared maximum. Memory64 shipped in Chrome 133, Firefox 134 and Node 24 while Safari has it only in a Technical Preview (P14-S58).
flags.correction: Use each WASM module's declared maximum memory as the limit (good <= 50%, bad >= 80%) and treat Safari as the constraining browser.

flags.claim: Rhino.Compute is not available to Educational licences (in general)
flags.detail: McNeel's page says only that core-hour billing is incompatible with Educational and Commercial licences and that Windows Server cannot take single-computer keys. It does not mention Rhino.Compute or workstation use.
flags.correction: Narrow the claim to what the page says; record workstation licensing as unverified.

flags.claim: Tower height (244-305 m) threshold status is 'verified'
flags.detail: The source P14-S54 is marked opened=false and the metric's own basis said the brief PDF was not opened, so the status contradicted the evidence. The brief's measurement convention is also unknown (CTBUH versus City base surface versus geodetic).
flags.correction: Status corrected; the range is unverified until the brief PDF is read, and the height is shown under three conventions in P14-M05.

flags.claim: Magnetic declination at the Vancouver site is about 15 degrees east (r1: informal; r2: computed)
flags.detail: r2: our own WMM2025 evaluation (NOAA coefficients from pygeomag's WMM_2025.COF, validated on pygeomag's Seattle example to 4 decimals) gives 15.37 degrees east at 49.2827 N, 123.1207 W for 2026.8 (derived). It has not been checked against NOAA's calculator, which was reported to need an API key; check one value by hand and record model, epoch and uncertainty.

flags.claim: Height limits inside the Queen Elizabeth Park view cones (3.2.1-3.2.4) and the CRS of City portal GeoJSON exports
flags.detail: The view-cones dataset has polygons only and points to by-laws; the City's view pages returned HTTP 403. The parcel, footprint and cone dataset metadata state no CRS (only the LiDAR page names its frame; the API returns lon/lat). Limits are hand-entered with source and status; see the r2 flag on the lon/lat frame test.

flags.claim: Hosted-LLM labelling is acceptable for competition entries
flags.detail: Anthropic states API inputs and outputs are deleted within 30 days by default, with zero retention only by agreement; whether the competition rules or the course allow sending project text to a hosted model is not known (the VTC terms read in r2 contain no AI rule; the FAQ only says to check the tool's terms). The labelling stage is opt-in per project, sends names and layers only, and a rules-only mode must work.

flags.claim: Core scope fits the time to 13 Nov 2026
flags.detail: r2 recompute from the module efforts: core about 19.5 person-days (M01 3.5, M02 7, M03 2, M04 3.5, M05 2, M07 1.5), not about 17; the entrant-ready slice for 6 Nov is about 18.0 (no IFC adapter). Capacity: 17 working days to 13 Nov (18 weekdays minus Remembrance Day, 11 Nov) and 13 to 6 Nov, for two students who also own other packets; nominal 34 and 26 person-days, so the slice needs about 70% of both students' time. Cut order if late: IFC adapter, normals and degenerate-face checks, SubD and curved fallback paths, table-only M04 UI.

flags.claim: EPSG:3157 can be registered in proj4js directly from the epsg.io PROJ string
flags.detail: The string +towgs84=-0.991,1.9072,0.5129,-1.25033e-07,-4.6785e-08,-5.6529e-08,0 carries the EPSG 1946 rotations in radians and in Coordinate Frame form, while proj4js multiplies +towgs84 rotations by SEC_TO_RAD (arc-seconds) and applies position-vector formulas, so the rotations are effectively dropped. Derived at the site: dropping them errs about 0.9 m (0.75 m east, 0.50 m south); a wrong sign errs about 1.8 m; a null shift versus the full EPSG 1946 shift differs by about 1.3 m. EPSG 1946 also ignores time-dependent parameters. Evidence: P14-S57, P14-S66, P14-S33, P14-S67.
flags.correction: Register +towgs84=-0.991,1.9072,0.5129,0.025790,0.009650,0.011660,0 (arc-seconds, position-vector sign, derived) or a null shift for City-to-City data, chosen by a LiDAR frame test, and unit-test both against PROJ to under 1 cm. Parcel agreement restated at 0.3 m good and 1.0 m bad.

flags.claim: Extrusion and SubD mesh access in rhino3dm is unconfirmed, and no Extrusion binding file exists
flags.detail: bnd_beam.cpp binds Extrusion with GetMesh, SetMesh and ToBrep (JS getMesh, setMesh, toBrep) and bnd_mesh.cpp binds Mesh.CreateFromSubDControlNet. These return cached meshes or a control-net approximation, and openNURBS has no tessellation, so a Brep or an extrusion saved without meshes stays unmeshed. Evidence: P14-S21, P14-S68.
flags.correction: Add a deterministic fallback mesher: exact prism for polyline-profile extrusions, earcut triangulation of planar Brep faces, SubD control net labelled 'volume biased', and a Rhino export how-to for the rest; block on unmeshed ProgramVolumes.

flags.claim: No source gives the downtown street-grid skew
flags.detail: The City parcel polygons cited as P14-S38 give it: 969 parcels within 700 m of 49.2827 N, 123.1207 W have edges of 15 m or more clustering at 44.6-44.8 degrees (mod 90) from true north, mean 44.7, so the street axes run at about 44.7 and 134.7 degrees (derived); parcel 669 Howe St shows 44.7 and 134.6-134.7.
flags.correction: Show the skew as a derived value (default 44.7 and 134.7 deg), keep it separate from UTM grid convergence (about 0.09 deg), and use it for an independent street-edge check of the true-north rotation. Which north the organiser's arrow shows stays unresolved.

flags.claim: Tower-height metric status 'false_assumption_corrected' reflects the evidence
flags.detail: The range was never shown to be false; it is unverified because the brief PDF has not been opened and the public page still links the brief to '#'. Evidence: P14-S53, P14-S54.
flags.correction: Status 'unverified'; the earlier wrong 'verified' label stays logged as the r1 FALSE ASSUMPTION flag above.

flags.claim: The direction of IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure between zone and spaces is unconfirmed
flags.detail: The IFC4.3 IfcSpatialZone page says spaces referenced by the zone use this relationship, and IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure has RelatingStructure (the spatial element within which objects are referenced) and RelatedElements; an 'IFC4 CHANGE' allows IfcSpace there, in particular for IfcSpatialZone. Evidence: P14-S03.
flags.correction: IfcSpatialZone is the RelatingStructure and its IfcSpaces the RelatedElements; reference each zone from its IfcBuilding too, and add bot:containsZone from the zone to its plates. Only the IFC4 ADD2 pages remain to confirm in the round-trip spike.

flags.claim: The north-type enum 'true, grid or magnetic' is unambiguous for a Vancouver designer
flags.detail: 'Grid' in the surveying sense is UTM grid north (convergence about 0.09 degrees here), but a designer reads it as street-grid or plan north, and the brief says the arrow is rotated relative to the street grid (about 44.7 degrees here, derived). Picking 'grid' would apply 0.09 degrees where about 45 are needed. Evidence: P14-S32, P14-S38.
flags.correction: Four plain-language types with a diagram: true north, magnetic north (about 15.4 degrees east, derived), projection (UTM) grid north, street-grid (plan) north.

flags.claim: The true-north error can be checked by comparing the arrow-derived bearing with a 'confirmed true north'
flags.detail: The confirmed value is usually taken from the same arrow, so the check is circular and cannot catch a wrong north type. Evidence: critique of round 2; P14-S38 gives an independent reference.
flags.correction: Check instead that the site's street-facing edges align with the parcel-derived street bearings after the chosen rotation (good <= 0.25 degree, bad >= 1 degree), and report the arrow-to-street angle (about 44.7 deg for a true or UTM-grid arrow, about 29.3 deg for a magnetic one).

flags.claim: Every ProgramVolume can be sliced into floor plates at every storey elevation without distorting area
flags.detail: Atria, double-height lobbies, sky gardens and the vertically extended public spaces the brief asks for would become stacked 'floor plates', inflating gross and FSR-counted area and distorting the 9.0 employment-FSR check. CTBUH also counts mezzanines, which slicing at storey heights misses. Evidence: P14-S34, P14-S03.
flags.correction: Add a per-volume floors-present list and FloorPlate.has_floor; count only floored plates in gross and counted FSR area, list void area apart, and map mezzanines to PARTIAL storeys.

flags.claim: The ground-to-grid scale factor can be stored in IfcMapConversion.Scale
flags.detail: IfcMapConversion.Scale applies one factor to x, y and z 'to convert units'; writing 0.9996 would also shrink heights (about 0.12 m on 300 m) and make viewers rescale the model. IFC4X3 ADD1 adds IfcMapConversionScaled with FactorX/Y/Z for coordinate scaling. Evidence: P14-S59.
flags.correction: Keep Scale = 1.0 in the IFC4 ADD2 export; store the grid factor in Layer 0 and a custom pset; use IfcMapConversionScaled with a Z factor of 1 for IFC4X3.

flags.claim: City portal GeoJSON lon/lat is true WGS84 rather than NAD83(CSRS) coordinates relabelled as WGS84
flags.detail: The dataset pages state no CRS. The two readings differ by about 1.3 m here (derived), the same size as the EPSG 1946 accuracy, so EPSG alone cannot decide. Test: reproject footprint corners both ways and compare with LiDAR 2022 building edges (native NAD83(CSRS) UTM 10). Relative positions among portal datasets are unaffected because they share one frame.

flags.claim: Sharing design states or forks before 30 Nov 2026 does not breach the VTC rule on previously published material
flags.detail: Terms clause 4.1 (read through a page tool) says visual materials must not have been previously published by the participant or team, while the FAQ says a previously published design may be resubmitted by its author. Whether private, team or public sharing of a design state counts is unconfirmed; public forks stay blocked by default. Ask the organiser by 3 Nov.

flags.claim: IFC4 ADD2 still carries IfcBuildingStorey.Elevation, IfcBuilding.ElevationOfRefHeight and IfcSite.RefElevation
flags.detail: Inferred from the IFC4.3 pages, which mark the first two deprecated in 4.3 and describe the third as the site reference height; the IFC4 ADD2 pages were not readable. The round-trip spike confirms.

flags.claim: The by-law definitions of floor area and site area (the FSR denominator) are known
flags.detail: The Zoning and Development By-law pages returned HTTP 403, so the denominator (brief rectangle 11,468 m2, drawn polygon or net parcel) and the excluded floor areas are unread; the tool records the choice beside counted_fsr_area.

flags.claim: Community-uploaded module code can run safely in the browser and under which project licence

Corrected: Rhino.Compute is MIT code but needs Rhino 8 for Windows and core-hour billing, not compatible with Educational licences; moved out of core.
Corrected: Rhino 8 and 9 index lists SketchUp, OBJ, FBX and glTF but not IFC or Revit; IFC via Rhino is not assumed.

Derived numbers (computed in round 1, not quoted): site area 11,468 m2 and 9.0 FSR about 103,200 m2; UTM area scale 0.08% about 83 m2; grid convergence about 0.1 deg at lon -123.12, lat 49.29; float32 step about 0.5 m at northing 5.46 million m.

notes:
Format routes: .3dm = rhino3dm.js/py (layers, names, ModelUnitSystem, EarthAnchorPoint); Breps need saved render meshes because openNURBS cannot tessellate, so r2 adds a fallback mesher (exact prism for polyline extrusions, earcut for planar faces, SubD control net) and blocks on unmeshed ProgramVolumes. OBJ = declared unit, no hierarchy. IFC = web-ifc in browser, IfcOpenShell server-side; IFC4X3 only after the round-trip spike. glTF/GLB = metres, Y-up, extras. FBX, DXF and Speckle/APS routes = v1. SketchUp = export OBJ/GLB (OBJ needs Pro), Speckle connector, or Rhino 8 import then save .3dm. Revit = IFC export, Speckle connector or APS (unverified).

Georeference: project CRS EPSG:3157 with arc-second position-vector shift or a null shift chosen by a LiDAR frame test; Z0 stored as geodetic elevation plus datum; four plain-language north types; street axes at about 44.7 and 134.7 degrees from true north (derived from 969 parcels); magnetic declination about 15.4 degrees east (derived).

Graph: Layer 0 is a staged document (Draft M02, Georef M03, Checked M05, Complete M04); M01 is a schema package, M07 a runtime service; DAG order M01, M07, M08, M02, M03, M05, M04, M06.

Schedule: core about 19.5 person-days against 17 working days to 13 Nov (Remembrance Day excluded); entrant-ready slice for 6 Nov about 18.0; capacity unknown. Publish a dated supported-formats list on 28 Oct, before registration closes on 29 Oct.

Q&A list to send by 31 Oct (closes 3 Nov): formats, units, CRS, vertical datum and Z0 of 'Site plans & 3D model'; which north the arrow shows; whether context and approved towers are included; height convention for 244-305 m; which uses count toward the 9.0 FSR and the site-area denominator; whether sharing work-in-progress design states counts as prior publication (terms 4.1); whether hosted AI labelling is allowed.

Anonymity: entries are judged anonymously and submitted as JPEG boards (terms 4.8), so P14-M06 scrubs shared model files and forks; board metadata belongs to PRES. Design states are private by default.

Sources: 73, above the target of about 40, because licence, cost and per-class IFC facts were needed per tool; 4 could not be opened (P14-S29, S54, S55, S56). The VTC terms were read through a page-to-text tool and need a person to re-check the clause numbers.
